Topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem: Fairness in a Divided World

Target audience: University students with a background in basic calculus and set theory

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Concept of Continuous Mapping

Lecture lines:
Continuous mapping links spheres to flat spaces.
Imagine stretching a globe onto a plane.
We must do this without any tearing.

Planned animations:
Visualize a continuous deformation of a shape, color #FFFFFF.
Highlight the preservation of neighborly points with a #FF5733 flash.
Show the boundary mapping closing upon itself, color #33FF57.

Section: section_2 — The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem (The Core Concept)

Lecture lines:
Borsuk-Ulam states spheres map to R-n.
Antipodal points share the same value.
Earth has two opposite spots with identical weather.

Planned animations:
Display a sphere surface, color #3498DB.
Identify two antipodal points, labeled A and B, color #E74C3C.
Pulse both points to show equal values, color #F1C40F.
Deform the sphere slightly to maintain the theorem, color #9B59B6.
Highlight the final mapping result, color #2ECC71.

Section: section_3 — Transition: From Geometry to Combinatorics

Lecture lines:
Topology helps us solve discrete problems.
Necklaces represent linear, ordered resource sets.
Cuts divide these sets into fair shares.

Planned animations:
Represent the geometric sphere as a discrete grid, color #BDC3C7.
Transform the continuous antipodal mapping into a combinatorial rule.
Highlight the shift to discrete binary choice, color #E67E22.

Section: section_4 — The Stolen Necklace Problem

Lecture lines:
Two thieves split a mixed bead necklace.
K plus S cuts ensure fair division.
Each thief receives identical bead types.
Raccoons demonstrate equal distribution of resources.
Fairness is guaranteed by simple cutting math.

Planned animations:
Display a necklace of beads with two colors, color #F39C12.
Animate a partition operation splitting the necklace, color #E74C3C.
Show the fair division of beads, color #2ECC71.
Reveal the theorem's requirement for two thieves, color #3498DB.
Finalize the split with visual equality check, color #FFFFFF.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Real-World Significance

Lecture lines:
Topology provides concrete guarantees for fairness.
Mathematical constraints force equitable resource allocation.
Useful for computing tasks and economics.

Planned animations:
Synthesize the previous geometric and combinatorial steps.
Reiterate the theorem's power with a bold summary text, color #FFFFFF.
Fade all elements to a clean, final conclusion state.

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Synthesis animation
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "D4")
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Final summary reveal
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_text))
        self.play(FadeOut(circle))
        self.wait(2)
